name: Elliptics
tagline: Reverbrain's DHT object store for medium and large files across datacenters, once used across Yandex services.
description: Elliptics is a distributed key-value object store created by Linux kernel developer Evgeniy Polyakov, first as part of the POHMELFS file system in 2007 and as a standalone project from 2008, later developed by his company Reverbrain. Keys hash into a distributed hash table within a group, and each group is a full replica that can live in a different datacenter, so reads survive the loss of whole sites without a central metadata server. It was built for objects from kilobytes to gigabytes, with the append-oriented Eblob on-disk backend, SLRU caching, streaming reads and writes, eventual recovery tools and server-side scripting. As of 2014 it backed Yandex Maps, Disk, Music and Photos. The last tagged release was in 2017 and the last commit in 2019, and reverbrain.com is offline.
statusNote: Last tag 2.26.11.1 (2017) and last commit 2019; Reverbrain's site is offline. Consider a maintained object store or Riak/Cassandra-class KV instead.

scale.notes: DHT per replica group, groups placed in separate datacenters; designed for billions of objects.

strengths: No central metadata server: placement is computed from the DHT ring
Replica groups in different datacenters keep serving when a site goes down
Eblob backend and streaming I/O suit objects from KB to multi-GB
Proven at Yandex scale for photos, music and disk storage
weaknesses: Unmaintained since 2019 with no vendor behind it
Eventual consistency with manual or scheduled recovery passes
Documentation was always thin and much of it lived on the now-dead vendor site
useCases: Running or migrating existing Elliptics clusters
notIdealFor: Workloads that need strong consistency or transactions
